page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.4xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores on an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core execution. Single-core metrics, such as stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores, fall into the bottom 25% tier. Similarly, single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression show weak to poor performance. However, multi-core benchmarks, including Geekbench multi-core, Passmark CPU, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, consistently achieve average tier results. Memory bandwidth tests show average performance for both small cached blocks and larger uncached blocks, though the Passmark memory score itself is positioned in the lower 25% tier.

Given its high memory density and average multi-core performance, the ecs.se1.4xlarge is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring large memory footprints without demanding top-tier single-thread CPU performance. It is suited for database operations, caching layers like Redis (achieving 11.3 million operations per second in testing), static web serving, and moderate multi-threaded processing. It is less suitable for single-threaded computational tasks or heavy LLM inference workloads.
